lead.headline: A fake Claude Code extension in Cursor's marketplace tried to plant an SSH backdoor
lead.summary: Versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 of Anthropic.claude-code, not built by Anthropic, sat in Cursor's extension marketplace on 29 Oct from about 2:27am to 1:35pm PT for Windows and macOS. The payload grabbed host details (hostname, user, git email, env var names, public IP), added an attacker SSH key labelled svc-telemetry and tried to open a reverse SSH tunnel with persistence; the SSH step mostly failed without admin rights. Cursor pulled it, rebuilt the marketplace and rotated keys. Microsoft says the bad builds never reached the VS Marketplace or npm. If you were exposed, uninstalling isn't enough: check ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, remove the persistence and rotate credentials.

number_of_day.label: AI API calls in 13 hours on one stolen Bedrock key, after a wave of breaches hit nine AI developer platforms this month.

news.headline: Wiz calls it Black October: nine AI dev platforms breached in a month
news.summary: Fireworks, Zeabur, Lightning AI, OpenCode, Railway, Warp, Northflank and others were hit, with attackers hunting stored env vars for AI keys to resell. Zeabur is shutting down, and Northflank tells users to assume every env var was decrypted.

news.headline: Cracks in the AI spending boom: Alphabet has its worst day on record
news.summary: Big Tech plans over $740B in capex. Alphabet fell 12% on Thursday after $9.1B of negative free cash flow in Q3, and on Friday the Nasdaq dropped 2.9% and Nvidia 4%.

news.headline: Google's first data-centre satellite is online and writing haiku
news.summary: The Suncatcher prototype carries four TPUs (one runs at a time, about 20 minutes per go) on up to 1 kW. Gemma 4 on board wrote a poem while it tests radiation and heat; two more satellites are planned for 2027.

news.headline: Finland and the US sign a Technology Prosperity Deal
news.summary: Valtonen and Rubio signed the memorandum in Washington on Thursday, covering AI exports, 5G/6G, quantum commercialisation, post-quantum cryptography and research security, alongside a critical minerals framework.

x_posts.name: Ethan Mollick
x_posts.text:
OpenAI kills a lot of its products

Sora lasted 6 months, Agent Builder 8 months, Group Chat 8 months, Atlas 9 months...

Most of the time (Sora excepted?) their own product became obsolete within months, in case you think they are immune to misjudging the exponential themselves
x_posts.why: A reminder to build on capabilities, not on any one product surface.

x_posts.name: Gergely Orosz
x_posts.text:
…When Railway was breached on 21 Oct, Northflank dunked on them and urged people to migrate over to them because of that breach.

9 days they got hacked, the same way.

Zero sympathy: instead of securing you were busy dunking
x_posts.why: The human side of the Black October breach wave.
